newsitem.title: INDIA: Oil flow to Indian Oil Assam refinery cut off.
newsitem.headline: Oil flow to Indian Oil Assam refinery cut off.

text.p: Suspected separatist guerrillas damaged a pipeline in northeastern India on Thursday, cutting off crude oil supplies to a refinery owned by Indian Oil Corp Ltd, police said.

Suspected members of the United Liberation Front of Assam (ULFA) damaged the main crude oil pipeline to the Barauni refinery in the eastern state of Bihar. Barauni has an annual processing capacity of 3.3 million tonnes.
"Oil flow to the Barauni refinery has been stopped following the damage," a senior official of state-run Oil India Ltd (OIL) told Reuters. "But the refinery has not been shut down so far."
United News of India said the militants had cut the pipeline with iron cutters.
Police said the damage had created a small oil spill which was later halted.
"The refinery has enough oil for the next two to three days," said the OIL official, who asked not to be identified. He did not say when he believed the oil flow would be restored.
Crude oil from the eastern area of nearby Assam state is pumped to the Barauni refinery through a 1,157 km (718 mile) pipeline.
Last year ULFA guerrillas bombed three oil pipelines some 50 km (30 miles) west of the Assam state capital Guwahati, forcing Barauni and another refinery to shut down temporarily.
The leftist ULFA is fighting a decade-old campaign for an independent socialist state. ULFA's main targets are officials, security forces and tea planters.
